answers.answer: First set the Timezone field in Settings, under Bot basics. Then use {schedule.next.at} for the day and start time, {schedule.next.date} for the day and date, or {schedule.next.full} for one line saying how long until it starts and when; all three show your channel's time zone. To show a viewer's own zone, use {schedule.next.viewerTime:<Region/City>} with one time zone name after the colon, such as America/New_York.
answers.quote: Your channel’s time zone is the Timezone field in Settings, under Bot basics.

answers.answer: You must already know how to use braces in a reply; if not, read Variables and templates first (first paragraph). You need a stream schedule kept on Twitch. You must set the Timezone field before using the helpers, because it starts as not set and times then show in UTC (Set your time zone first section). The bot needs no extra Twitch permission. For viewerTime you need a time zone database name made of a region, a slash and a city.
answers.quote: It starts as not set, and then times show in UTC, so set it before you use these helpers.

answers.answer: Success: the helper is replaced by a time like Friday 20:00 in your channel's zone. Failure shows in two ways. A helper that prints as typed means an unknown or missing zone name for viewerTime, a missing or out-of-range number for schedule.list, no stream left for schedule.next.*, or no answer from Twitch. An empty result means there is nothing to list. The concepts differ like this: at, date and full use the channel zone; in and relative count from now; viewerTime uses the zone you name.
answers.quote: A name the bot does not know, or no name at all, makes the helper print as typed, so check a new name once in your own chat.

answers.answer: During a vacation the next-stream helpers still show the first stream on the schedule that is not canceled and has not ended, even when it falls on a break day; they do not skip the break. So the reply should also name the break with {schedule.vacation.until}, for example: On a break until {schedule.vacation.until}. Next stream: {schedule.next.at}. If no stream that is not canceled is left inside the break, the viewer sees the first stream after the break; if one is left, they see that stream's day.
answers.quote: The next-stream helpers do not skip streams inside the break.

answers.answer: Only a small detour. I learned that the break reply needs changing back after the break only after I had already set it up; the cost is one later edit, and the page says exactly when and to what. I reread the table example Fri 15:00 against Friday 20:00 until the following paragraph explained that it is only a sample.
answers.quote: When the break is over, the first part reads On a break until ., so change the reply back to {schedule.next.full} at that point.

answers.answer: Nothing is materially confusing read aloud. The sentence explaining the viewerTime sample is needed only because the table example does not match the other rows; it costs one extra sentence but stops a wrong conclusion.
answers.quote: The example above is only a sample of the shape: a time of day in the zone you name, not a conversion for your own stream.
